authoredSolutions.2: Let \(m_{1}\) arrive with speed \(u\) and let both bodies leave with speed \(v\), \(m_{1}\) moving back. Momentum: \(m_{1}u = -m_{1}v + m_{2}v = (m_{2} - m_{1})v\). The bodies separate at \(2v\) and approached at \(u\), so \(2v = eu\), where \(e \leq 1\) is the coefficient of restitution. Then \(m_{1}u = (m_{2} - m_{1})\frac{eu}{2}\), so \(\frac{m_{2}}{m_{1}} = 1 + \frac{2}{e} \geq 3\). The roots of \(x^{2}+x+1=0\) are the complex cube roots of unity \(\omega,\omega^{2}\), which satisfy \(\omega^{3}=1\). Since \(x^{2}+x+1\) divides \(P(x)\), both roots make \(P\) vanish:
\[P(\omega)=f(\omega^{3})+\omega\,g(\omega^{3})=f(1)+\omega\,g(1)=0,\]
\[P(\omega^{2})=f(\omega^{6})+\omega^{2} g(\omega^{6})=f(1)+\omega^{2} g(1)=0.\]
Subtracting gives \((\omega-\omega^{2})g(1)=0\); as \(\omega\neq\omega^{2}\), we get \(g(1)=0\), and hence \(f(1)=0\). Therefore
\[P(1)=f(1)+1\cdot g(1)=0+0=0.\]

\[P^{3}=2P-I,\quad P^{4}=2I-3P,\quad P^{5}=5P-3I,\]
\[P^{6}=P\cdot P^{5}=5P^{2}-3P=5(I-P)-3P=5I-8P.\]
Hence \(P^{n}=5I-8P\) holds for \(n=6\).
